subject.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout

question: Should a Discord listener that exceeds `listenerTimeout` retain its `maxConcurrency` slot indefinitely, even though enough permanently hung listeners can stop all subsequent gateway listener work?
rationale: Promises cannot be forcibly cancelled, so the implementation must deliberately choose between exceeding the configured execution bound after timeout and risking complete queue saturation; tests cannot resolve which operational contract maintainers want.

options.title: Enforce the true execution bound
options.body: Retain the slot until listener settlement, but add saturation observability, document the availability tradeoff, and require real-runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve timeout capacity release
options.body: Keep current behavior and clarify that `maxConcurrency` bounds active dispatch accounting rather than uncancellable background listener execution.

options.title: Design cancellation first
options.body: Pause this patch and introduce an abortable listener contract before making timeout release both execution capacity and underlying work.

recommendation.title: Enforce the true execution bound
recommendation.body: Retain the slot until listener settlement, but add saturation observability, document the availability tradeoff, and require real-runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person most directly to the original Discord parallel-handler queue contract.
